complexity.notes: The algorithm is the right shape, but `p[1] in starts`, `starts.remove(...)`, and `parent[w].remove(v)` are linear scans, so the whole thing runs in O(n * m) instead of the O(n + m) this approach can reach; swapping them for ||a set for the zero-dependency courses and integer counts in place of the parent lists|| closes that gap. Otherwise clean, and dropping the O(m) `prerequisites.remove(...)` scan from the previous version was a good fix.
complexity.summary: A reverse Kahn's-style elimination: it builds prerequisite/dependent adjacency maps, starts from courses nothing depends on, and repeatedly removes a course from its prerequisites' dependent lists; if every entry gets removed there is no cycle.
